passages.text: The first telegraph cable laid across the Atlantic Ocean, completed in 1858, carried signals so weakly that a message of fewer than one hundred words took about sixteen hours to send. ______ the cable stopped working entirely after only about three weeks.

content.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
content.explanation: The first sentence describes one problem with the cable (it was extremely slow). The second adds a further problem (it soon stopped working). "Moreover" signals that additional, related information follows.

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: "In other words" introduces a restatement, but failing after three weeks is a new point, not a rewording of the slow signals.

distractorRationales.label: C
distractorRationales.text: "For example" introduces an instance of a general claim, but the cable's failure isn't an example of its slowness.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: "Instead" signals a replacement or alternative, which doesn't fit two problems that both occurred.

passages.text: Many people believe that bats are blind, an idea reflected in the familiar phrase "blind as a bat." ______ every known species of bat can see, and some fruit bats rely heavily on their keen eyesight to find food at dusk.

content.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
content.explanation: The first sentence presents a common belief (bats are blind). The second sentence contradicts it (all bats can see). "However" signals that the next idea contrasts with the one before it.

distractorRationales.label: A
distractorRationales.text: "Similarly" signals a comparable idea, but the second sentence contradicts the first rather than resembling it.

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: "For instance" introduces an example of the previous claim, but bats' ability to see is not an example of the belief that they are blind.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: "Therefore" signals a result, but the fact that bats can see does not follow from people believing they are blind.

distractorRationales.label: A
distractorRationales.text: "Nevertheless" signals something that happened despite the previous point, but the disease is a consequence of the wet conditions, not something that happened in spite of them.

distractorRationales.label: C

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: "For example" introduces an example of a general claim, but the first sentence makes no general claim that the diseased tomatoes illustrate.

passages.text: Architect Lena Okafor designs buildings that respond to the climate around them rather than relying mainly on machines for heating and cooling. ______ her public library in a hot, dry region uses thick earthen walls that absorb heat during the day and slowly release it during the cool desert nights.

content.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

The second describes one specific building that follows this approach (earthen walls that manage heat naturally). "For example" introduces a specific case that illustrates a general claim.

distractorRationales.label: A
distractorRationales.text: "Even so" signals that what follows happens despite the previous point, but the library fits Okafor's approach rather than going against it.

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: "By contrast" signals a difference, but the library is consistent with Okafor's climate-based design, not different from it.

distractorRationales.label: C
distractorRationales.text: "In addition" introduces a separate, new point, but the library is not a new point; it is an illustration of the approach already described.

content.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

distractorRationales.label: C

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: "Similarly" signals a comparable situation, but the second novel's success is the opposite of the first book's reception.

passages.text: Ecologist Tomas Reyes compared two populations of the same species of wildflower growing on a mountain in Colorado. content.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
content.explanation: The passage compares two groups: short plants on the windy ridge and much taller plants in the sheltered valley. "By contrast" signals that the second sentence describes a group that differs from the first.

distractorRationales.label: A
distractorRationales.text: "Furthermore" adds another point in the same direction, but the valley plants' height contrasts with the ridge plants' small size.

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: "As a result" signals a consequence, but the ridge plants' short height does not cause the valley plants to grow tall.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: "For instance" introduces an example of the previous claim, but tall valley plants are not an example of short ridge plants.

distractorRationales.label: A

distractorRationales.label: C

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: "Regardless" signals that something happens no matter what came before, but pressing the paper depends on the block having been inked.

passages.text: When the city of Harlow Falls replaced street parking on Main Avenue with protected bike lanes, many shop owners warned that customers would stop coming. Economist Priya Natarajan tracked sales at those shops. In the first two months, sales dipped slightly, much as the owners had feared. ______ by the end of the first year, sales at the shops had risen 9 percent, outpacing sales at shops on similar streets that had kept their parking.

content.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
content.explanation: The early dip matched the owners' fears, but the final sentence describes a later outcome that goes the other way: sales rose and beat comparable streets. "Ultimately, though" signals both a later point in time and a reversal of the earlier trend.

distractorRationales.label: A
distractorRationales.text: "Predictably" suggests the rise was expected, but the owners had predicted losses, so a 9 percent gain was the opposite of what they predicted.

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: "Accordingly" signals a consequence that fits what came before, but rising sales do not follow from an early dip; they reverse it.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: "In the same way" signals a parallel to the previous sentence, but a rise in sales is not parallel to a dip in sales.

passages.text: Literary scholar Ana Brandt argues that the letters of nineteenth-century field naturalists deserve to be read as literature, not merely mined as scientific records. ______ she acknowledges that most of the letters were dashed off in haste and lack the careful polish of published essays; her point is that their vivid, unplanned descriptions of wildlife have an artistry of their own.

distractorRationales.text: "Consequently" signals a result, but Brandt's admission that the letters lack polish does not follow from her argument that they are literature.

distractorRationales.label: C
distractorRationales.text: "For example" introduces support for the previous claim, but hasty, unpolished writing is a limitation, not an example of the letters' literary value.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: "Moreover" adds a point that strengthens the previous claim, but the admission that the letters lack polish cuts against Brandt's claim before she answers it.

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: "Likewise" signals a similar point, but a tiny shift is the opposite of the noticeable shift described in the previous sentence.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: "In short" introduces a summary, but the last sentence reports a new finding instead of summarizing what came before.
